extracted.intended_audience: military legal officers, quartermaster officials, Department of War counsel, and government administrators responsible for disposition of public/military property and personnel rank matters
extracted.subtask_description: Digest of legal holdings and administrative rules governing disposition of public/military property (sales, condemnations, proceeds, uses) and principles for attachment, computation, and effects of military rank (actual, relative, lineal, brevet, suspension). Intended as a reference for officials implementing or advising on these matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statutory authorization required for sale of timber on military reservations
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no statute which would authorize the sale of timber on military reservations, and in the absence of such a statute the Secretary of War cannot authorize such sale.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exception — damaged or deteriorating timber may be sold under section 1241
rubrics_metrics.description: Timber which has reached maturity, so that it begins to deteriorate, may be regarded as damaged and unsuitable, and may be sold under the provisions of section 1241 R.S.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also applies to timber thrown down and injured by a tornado if inspection/survey finds it unsuitable; holdings: C. 20531, Oct. 15, 1906; 25236, July 8, 1909 and Apr. 1, 1910; 25558, Sept. 14, 1909, and Oct. 4, 1910; 20544, Nov., 1906; 20818, Dec. 22, 1906.

rubrics_metrics.name: Driftwood and value-bearing materials on reservations treated as War Department property
rubrics_metrics.description: Driftwood coming ashore on a military reservation, if it has any value, must be treated as other property under the control of the War Department.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contract for clearing reservation where contractor acquires timber as incident of sale
rubrics_metrics.description: Where for sanitary reasons it was necessary to clear a reservation of timber and underbrush, a contract may properly be entered into providing that the timber and underbrush shall become the property of the contractor; the clearing is regarded as incident to the sale of the timber/underbrush under section 1241 R.S.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authority to sell damaged or unsuitable military stores — sale on credit permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: In view of the general authority vested in the President and Secretary of War by the provision in regard to the sale of military stores damaged or unsuitable for the public service (act of March 3, 1825; now sec. 1241, R.S.), such stores may legally be sold on credit if such mode of disposition is deemed for the public interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Payment of auctioneer commissions from sale proceeds — limits
rubrics_metrics.description: A noncommissioned officer who acted as auctioneer at a public sale of condemned quartermaster stores cannot legally be paid out of the proceeds of the sale a commission (e.g., 10%) or any other compensation for such services absent statutory authority; pay/allowances of enlisted men are fixed by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Holdings: P. 60, 363, July, 1893; 62, 95, Oct., 1893. By contrast, a civilian employee hired by the Quartermaster's Department whose pay is not fixed by law/regulations may legally be paid for auctioneer services. C. 2567, Sept., 1896; 6988, Sept., 1899; 11983, Feb. 1, 1902.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transaction characterized as contract settlement (not sale) when barrels to be returned
rubrics_metrics.description: Where oil was purchased in barrels with the understanding that the empty barrels should be returned at an agreed valuation, the transaction is not a sale but a settlement under contract, and therefore no inspection would be required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of condemned property for experiments or other departmental purposes permitted
rubrics_metrics.description: There is no legal objection to granting permission for medical experiments on condemned cavalry horses where results are to be embodied in departmental reports; condemned cannon may be used for casting bronze tablets; condemned searchlight's sale may be deferred for loan to an institution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C. 3792, Jan. 17, 1898 (veterinary experiments); C. 25359, July 21, 1909 (cannon); C. 25236, Mar. 18 and Apr. 1, 1910 (searchlight loan and sale deferment). The requirements of the statute are directory to the extent of vesting incidents of the sale, including the date, in the discretion of the Secretary of War.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposit of proceeds into Treasury under section 3618 — 'net proceeds' rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 3618 R.S. requires that 'all proceeds of sales of old material, condemned stores, supplies, or other public property of any kind' shall, with specified exceptions, be deposited and covered into the Treasury as miscellaneous receipts and not withdrawn except by statutory appropriation; the statute as amended requires the 'net proceeds' only to be deposited, so expenses of sale should be paid from the proceeds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Held that proceeds of surplus cuttings of material for clothing manufactured by Quartermaster's Dept. are not within exceptions and must be deposited; if no sale takes place, advertising costs are a proper charge against the appropriation for contingencies of the Army. C. 25236, Mar. 18, 1910; R. 42, 653, May, 1880.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-public-property classification — post library books exception
rubrics_metrics.description: Books for a post library purchased out of post exchange funds or donated to the library are not 'public property' within the meaning of section 3618, R.S.; proceeds from their sale may legally be expended in the purchase of new books.

rubrics_metrics.name: Disposition of funds from sales of property belonging to special funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the property was not public property of the United States but pertained to a road fund or the District of Alaska (to be used and expended on its behalf), the moneys received from sales should be applied to the purposes for which the fund was appropriated by Congress.

rubrics_metrics.name: Secretary of War may fix price for disposal of used/repaired property not covered by sec.1241
rubrics_metrics.description: Where property not covered by section 1241 R.S. is to be disposed of, if the property has been in use and repaired so that its value is less than its cost, the Secretary of War may fix a price at which the property shall be disposed of.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on sale/barter of soldiers' arms and effect beyond Civil War
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of section 23, chapter 75, act of March 3, 1863, prohibiting the sale, etc., of their arms, etc., by soldiers, and declaring that no right of property or possession shall be acquired thereby, are not limited to the Civil War period but remain in force; an officer may seize arms disposed of contrary to the prohibition wherever found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R. 22, 525, Dec., 1866. Advice: before making seizures, officers should assure themselves that parties in possession have not acquired title in a legal manner. R. 29, 187 and 291, Aug., 1869; C. 11219, Sept. 12, 1901.

rubrics_metrics.name: Section 3748 — prohibition and seizure of clothing furnished to soldiers
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 3748 R.S. provides that clothing furnished by the United States to a soldier shall not be bartered, exchanged, pledged, loaned or given away, and a civilian in possession of such clothing is presumptive evidence of sale; such property may be summarily seized by any officer of the United States and delivered to quartermaster or authorized officer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The language indicates summary seizure is authorized and no court process is required; however, asserting rights through the courts is also permissible and may be preferable in many cases. C. 5303, Nov., 1898.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rank is not an office but may be attached to an office
rubrics_metrics.description: Rank is not an office — it may be attached to an office. Offices may have attached ranks (e.g., Chief of the Record and Pension Office having been given ranks at different times).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C. 6020, Mar. 10, 1899; 19425, Mar. 17, 1906; 4747, Aug. 6, 1898; 17508, Feb. 15, 1905. Note: some officers (e.g., veterinarians, paymasters' clerks) are officers without rank under statute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dates determining rank (three-date rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: There are three dates from which the rank and precedence of an officer of the regular establishment may be determined: (1) date of appointment/commission; (2) date of acceptance of the appointment; (3) a date anterior established by the date of rank conferred in the appointment/commission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: C. 23135, Apr. 3, 1909. An accepted appointment takes effect as to rank from the date it is completed by the signature of the appointing power unless the appointment specifies a fixed date for attachment of rank.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rank may relate back to date of vacancy
rubrics_metrics.description: The rank of an officer may relate back to the date of the occurrence of the vacancy to which the commission has reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative rank determined by time of service as commissioned officer
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1219 R.S. provides a rule for determining relative rank of officers of the same grade and date of appointment by reference to time of service; the time of service as a commissioned officer in the Army is alone to be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorities: P. 40, 51, Mar., 1890; numerous opinions and compilations (see citations).

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative rank generally fixed and immutable except by limited means
rubrics_metrics.description: Relative rank once fixed cannot be changed except by act of Congress, pursuant to the sentence of a general court-martial, or by the pardoning power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brevet rank rules — conferral and limited effect
rubrics_metrics.description: Brevet rank can properly neither be conferred nor take effect except as an incident of full rank of a lower grade; an officer assigned to duty according to brevet rank may exercise the authority and privileges of such rank only for the purposes of that command/duty and during its continuance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: R. 21, 608, Aug., 1866; C. 2122, Mar. 10, 1896; 12419, Apr. 14, 1902. When assigned, brevet rank becomes actual military rank for period of assignment, but some privileges (e.g., aids-de-camp) may require Secretary of War authority. R. 42, 21, Oct., 1878.

rubrics_metrics.name: Suspension from rank does not deprive right to rise in files
rubrics_metrics.description: Suspension from rank does not deprive the officer of the right to rise in files in his grade (e.g., upon promotion of the senior officer) and does not affect rights previously vested.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Discussion: suspension does not affect the office; loss of files is a continuing punishment and treating suspension as affecting files would be contrary to principles of military law. R. 33, 69, 109, June, 1872.

rubrics_metrics.name: Warrant as evidence of rank for noncommissioned officers; replacement rules
rubrics_metrics.description: A warrant is evidence of the rank held by a noncommissioned officer; if lost without fault of the officer it may be replaced with notation assigning rank back of the date of original appointment to the grade which carries the rank in question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Volunteer officers' relative rank dating (statutory variations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Relative rank of volunteer officers may be dated from their date of appointment or, under other provisions, may be determined by date of acceptance or muster; different acts (e.g., April 22, 1898; March 3, 1899) and contexts produce differing rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Two officers commissioned as volunteers on same date — relative rank determined by date of acceptance of original commissions (C. 4254, June 3, 1898; 7282, Nov. 15, 1899; 7790, Mar. 8, 1900). Under April 22, 1898 provisions, relative rank dated from date of appointment (C. 4139, May 18, 1898).

rubrics_metrics.name: Loss of files as sentence affects lineal and relative rank
rubrics_metrics.description: A sentence to lose files or be reduced on the regimental list results in loss of lineal and corresponding relative Army rank; such a sentence is a continuing punishment removable by pardon unless fully executed and rendered irrevocable by subsequent events.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Illustrations and holdings: P. 47, 293, May, 1891; R. 55, 620, June, 1888; P. 29, 487, Jan., 1889; P. 41, 380, July, 1890.
